target_variable: surface water quality class (6 classes, I to worse than V) from 9 online-monitored indicators
notes: Model = Auto-sklearn ensemble. Borderline domain/task: target class is a deterministic single-factor rule of the same indicators measured at ~1900 national monitoring sites (CNEMC), so it is not spatial mapping from covariates. Spatial F1 slightly higher than random for most models. Logistic regression (0.6457 vs 0.6453) not extracted. Sampling: 50,000 stratified-random subset of 10.16 M records from monitoring network (unknown design).

target_variable: seasonal Landsat NDVI (forecast of next-season NDVI from 35-year series)
notes: BORDERLINE comparator. 200,000 global tiles (sampled around populous cities -> clustered) K-means clustered on lat/lon into 100 spatial blocks; whole blocks assigned to Pool A (177,523 locations: train 157,523, val_id 8,000, OOD-t 12,000) or Pool B (22,477, spatial OOD). Random comparator = OOD-t: held-out Pool A locations (not used in training, but within the same K-means blocks as training locations; assignment presumably random, not explicitly stated) predicting the same target years as OOD-st; spatial = OOD-st: Pool B locations in blocks fully separated from training. Both splits share the same temporal shift (input 1990-2022, predict 2023/2024), so the only design difference is spatial separation. In-distribution val_id (2022) results not reported; OOD-s 2022 only spatial (Table V). Spatial scores are BETTER than random here; authors note Pool B over-represents Arid (61.8% vs 48.6%) and Shrubland, single allocation draw. Bias also reported in Table V only. Non-ML baselines (persistence, climatology, linear trend, Kalman filter) not extracted. n_samples = all 200,000 locations; test sets 12,000 (OOD-t) and 22,477 (OOD-st).
